description: Swedish Financial Supervisory Authority. Supervises banks, insurance companies, securities firms, and other financial entities. Primary AML/CFT supervisor for Swedish obliged entities. Issues licences, publishes supervisory guidance, conducts AML inspections, and imposes sanctions. Reports to Swedish Ministry of Finance.

Finnish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finanssivalvonta). AML/CFT supervisor for Finnish obliged entities including banks, payment institutions, and investment firms. Operates under the Bank of Finland. Conducts supervisory inspections, issues AML guidance, and cooperates in EBA/AMLA colleges.

Norwegian Financial Supervisory Authority. AML/CFT supervisor for Norwegian obliged entities. Norway is an EEA member — implements AMLD5 via EEA agreement. Finanstilsynet publishes AML supervisory reports, conducts on-site inspections, and cooperates with Scandinavian peers. Key guidance: Finanstilsynet AML supervisory circular series.

Danish Financial Supervisory Authority. AML/CFT supervisor for Danish obliged entities. Administers Danish Hvidvaskloven enforcement. Conducts risk-based AML inspections and publishes supervisory reports. Notable: significant AML enforcement action against Danske Bank (2018-2022 scandal).

Swedish Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) within the National Police Authority (Polismyndigheten). Receives and analyses suspicious transaction reports (STR/SAR) from Swedish obliged entities. Disseminates financial intelligence to law enforcement. Participates in Egmont Group. Key unit: Section for financial intelligence (FIPO).

canonical_name: KRP / FIVA — Finnish FIU (National Bureau of Investigation)
description: Finnish Financial Intelligence Unit within the National Bureau of Investigation (Keskusrikospoliisi, KRP). Receives and analyses STRs/SARs from Finnish obliged entities. Disseminates intelligence to Finnish law enforcement and authorities. Operates goAML reporting system.

Norwegian Economic Crime Unit (Økokrims hvitvaskingsenhet) functioning as national FIU. Receives STRs from Norwegian obliged entities under Hvitvaskingsloven. Analyses and disseminates intelligence. Also functions as specialist prosecutor for economic crime including ML.

Danish FIU (Hvidvasksekretariatet) within the State Prosecutor for Serious Economic and International Crime (SØIK/Statsadvokaten for Særlig Kriminalitet). Receives and analyses STRs from Danish obliged entities. Part of Egmont Group.

Under AMLA Regulation 2024/1620, AMLA will establish supervisory colleges for cross-border financial groups. Nordic supervisors (FI SE, FIN-FSA, Finanstilsynet NO, Finanstilsynet DK) participate in colleges for cross-border groups active in Nordic markets. AMLA chairs colleges where DSEs are involved.

FI's published AML supervisory guidance and expectations. Key publications: FI's general guidelines on AML (FFFS series), supervisory inspections of AML frameworks, risk assessment guidance. FI has issued significant fines: Swedbank (4 BSEK, 2020), SEB (1 BSEK, 2020), Nordea. FI approach: risk-based, proportionate, outcome-focused.

Finanstilsynet (NO) AML supervisory circulars, thematic reviews, and inspection reports. Key publications: Rundskriv series on AML/CFT. Norway implements AMLD5 via EEA. Finanstilsynet thematic review on real estate AML (2020), virtual currency (2021), and DNB correspondence banking (2019).

Finanstilsynet (DK) AML supervisory guidance and enforcement actions. Key context: Danske Bank non-resident portfolio scandal (2007-2015, EUR 200bn flagged flows via Estonia branch). Significant regulatory response: strengthened AML inspections, enhanced reporting requirements, Hvidvaskloven amendments. FT DK coordinates with Estonian FSA and international regulators.

FI SE supervisory inspection process for AML/CFT: (1) Risk-based selection of supervised entities; (2) Off-site preparation (document requests, FFFS review); (3) On-site inspection (interviews, sample testing); (4) Supervisory communication and findings; (5) Sanction decision if warranted (remark, warning, licence revocation, fine). FI can impose administrative fines up to 5 BSEK or 10% turnover.

Suspicious Activity Report (SAR) / Suspicious Transaction Report (STR) filing across Nordic FIUs: SE→Finanspolisen (via portal), FI→KRP via goAML, NO→Økokrim (HVITVASK portal), DK→Hvidvasksekretariatet. Each FIU has different technical platform and threshold guidance. AMLR will harmonise SAR format across EU (Finland/DK/SE) but Norway (EEA, not EU) will follow EEA equivalent.

AMLR (Regulation 2024/1624) is directly applicable in SE, FI, DK from July 2027. AMLR supersedes national CDD, monitoring, and SAR provisions in Penningtvättslagen (SE), Finnish ML Act (FI), Hvidvaskloven (DK). Norway (EEA) will implement equivalent via EEA agreement — Hvitvaskingsloven will be amended. AMLD6 transposition deadline: July 2027.

Nordic supervisors (FI SE, FIN-FSA, FT DK) formally adopted EBA/GL/2021/02 (Risk Factors Guidelines) and EBA/GL/2021/05 (Internal Governance). FI SE and FIN-FSA participate in EBA AML Standing Committee. Finanstilsynet NO complies as EEA — EBA guidelines integrated into Norwegian supervisory expectations via Finanstilsynet circulars.

FATF mutual evaluations of Nordic jurisdictions: Sweden (5th round 2017 — largely compliant, effective on most IO), Finland (5th round 2019 — substantial effectiveness), Norway (4th round 2014, 5th round follow-up ongoing), Denmark (5th round 2017 — significant improvements needed in some areas). Results drive supervisory priority-setting.

FI SE enforcement tools under Swedish law: (1) Remark (anmärkning) — minor breach; (2) Warning (varning) — significant breach; (3) Licence revocation (återkallelse av tillstånd); (4) Administrative fine (sanktionsavgift) up to the higher of 5 BSEK / EUR 5M or 10% of annual turnover. Public disclosure of sanctions is standard. Notable: Swedbank 2020 (4 BSEK AML fine), SEB 2020 (1 BSEK).

canonical_name: Nordic Supervisory Expectations — Business-Wide Risk Assessment
description: Nordic supervisors consistently require documented Business-Wide Risk Assessments (BWRA). SE/FI/DK: required under national AML law (Penningtvättslagen Ch.2, Finnish ML Act s.6-7, Hvidvaskloven s.7). AMLR Art.10 will codify BWRA at EU level. Nordic supervisory inspections routinely assess quality of BWRA documentation, methodology, and ML/TF risk factor coverage.
